	LPD6803   = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::LPD6803),   ///< LPD6803 LED chipset
	LPD8806   = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::LPD8806),   ///< LPD8806 LED chipset
	WS2801    = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::WS2801),    ///< WS2801 LED chipset
	WS2803    = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::WS2803),    ///< WS2803 LED chipset
	SM16716   = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::SM16716),   ///< SM16716 LED chipset
	P9813     = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::P9813),     ///< P9813 LED chipset
	APA102    = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::APA102),    ///< APA102 LED chipset
	SK9822    = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::SK9822),    ///< SK9822 LED chipset
	SK9822HD  = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::SK9822HD),  ///< SK9822 LED chipset with 5-bit gamma correction
	DOTSTAR   = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::DOTSTAR),   ///< APA102 LED chipset alias
	DOTSTARHD = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::DOTSTARHD), ///< APA102HD LED chipset alias
	APA102HD  = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::APA102HD),  ///< APA102 LED chipset with 5-bit gamma correction

	HD108     = static_cast<int>(fl::SpiChipset::HD108),     ///< 16-bit variant of HD107, always gamma corrected. No SD (standard definition) option available - all HD108s use gamma correction, and a non-gamma corrected version is not planned.
};

objects.description: Enum of parallel/blockless output port configurations used by the blockless/inline-parallel controllers. Members depend on platform macros indicating available ports.
Function pointer type for power-scaling callbacks used by CFastLED to limit brightness based on a power budget. Signature: uint8_t func(uint8_t scale, uint32_t data).

Global FastLED manager class. Owns global brightness, FPS tracking, power limiting model/callback, and provides numerous addLeds/addChannel helpers that construct/register concrete controllers. Exposes platform driver management on ESP32. Lifetime: a single global instance FastLED is declared extern here and defined in the library. Stores a power_func and power budget data, and touches controller list via static functions.
Extern declaration of the global CFastLED manager instance used by sketches via the name FastLED.

functions.name: CFastLED::CFastLED
functions.description: Constructs the global FastLED controller manager. Initializes internal state such as global brightness, FPS tracking, and power management fields. Typically instantiated as the global FastLED object.
requirements: Called implicitly via the global FastLED instance; users normally do not construct directly.
No arguments.

functions.name: CFastLED::init
functions.description: Performs one-time platform-specific initialization for FastLED subsystems. Safe to call multiple times (subsequent calls are no-ops). On ESP32, initializes channel/SPI bus managers; on other platforms it may be a no-op.
requirements: May be called at any time before using FastLED to force early initialization.
Safe to call multiple times; no side effects after the first initialization.

functions.name: CFastLED::addListener
functions.description: Registers a listener to receive engine events (e.g., begin/end of frame/show). Disabled on AVR to save space.
requirements: listener must point to a valid fl::EngineEvents::Listener instance.
Do not pass a dangling pointer; the listener must outlive its registration until removed.

functions.name: CFastLED::removeListener
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered engine event listener.
requirements: listener must be the same instance previously passed to addListener.
Removing a listener that was not added is unspecified; ensure it was registered.

functions.name: CFastLED::onBeginFrame
functions.description: Manually triggers the begin-frame engine event. Normally invoked automatically by show() unless FASTLED_MANUAL_ENGINE_EVENTS is defined.
requirements: Only needed when FASTLED_MANUAL_ENGINE_EVENTS is defined; otherwise show() triggers it automatically.

functions.name: CFastLED::onEndShowLeds
functions.description: Manually triggers the end-of-show engine event. Normally invoked automatically by show() unless FASTLED_MANUAL_ENGINE_EVENTS is defined.
requirements: Only needed when FASTLED_MANUAL_ENGINE_EVENTS is defined; otherwise show() triggers it automatically.

functions.name: CFastLED::addLeds
functions.signature: static ::CLEDController & CFastLED::addLeds(::CLEDController *pLed, CRGB *data, int nLedsOrOffset, int nLedsIfOffset = 0)
functions.description: Registers an existing CLEDController with FastLED and associates it with a CRGB pixel buffer. Supports two forms: 3-arg where nLedsOrOffset is the count; 4-arg where nLedsOrOffset is the offset into data and nLedsIfOffset is the count.
requirements: pLed must be a valid pointer to a CLEDController (non-null) that remains alive for the program lifetime or until explicitly removed (auto-removal not provided here).
data must point to a buffer of CRGB elements large enough for the configured number of LEDs plus any offset.
If nLedsIfOffset == 0, nLedsOrOffset is interpreted as the LED count; otherwise nLedsOrOffset is the offset and nLedsIfOffset is the LED count.
Offset and counts must not cause out-of-bounds access on data.

functions.name: CFastLED::addLedChannel
functions.description: Registers a Channel-based LED controller (created via Channel::create<ENGINE>(config)) with FastLED. Channels already link themselves into the controller list; this returns the same shared_ptr for convenience.
requirements: channel must be a valid, non-null ChannelPtr created by Channel::create.
Caller should retain the returned shared_ptr to control lifetime.

functions.name: CFastLED::addChannel
functions.description: Creates and registers a runtime-configured Channel-based controller from the provided configuration and returns a shared_ptr to it. Controller auto-registers on creation and auto-removes on destruction. Marked [[nodiscard]].
requirements: config must be valid for the chosen platform/engine (pin, timing, buffer, order).
Caller must store the returned ChannelPtr to manage lifetime (function is [[nodiscard]]).
Supported platforms for channel engines include ESP32 variants as noted; returns nullptr if unsupported.

functions.name: CFastLED::setBrightness
functions.description: Sets the global brightness scaling factor applied during show().
requirements: scale is an 8-bit value (0–255).

functions.name: CFastLED::getBrightness
functions.description: Returns the current global brightness scaling factor.

functions.name: CFastLED::setDriverEnabled
functions.description: ESP32: Enables or disables a named channel driver (e.g., "RMT", "SPI", "PARLIO"). Non-ESP32: No-op stub.
requirements: On ESP32, name must match a registered driver (case-sensitive).
Takes effect on the next LED update.
On non-ESP32 platforms this function does nothing.

functions.name: CFastLED::setExclusiveDriver
functions.description: ESP32: Disables all channel drivers and enables only the named one. Useful for testing/debugging specific drivers. Non-ESP32: Always returns false.
requirements: On ESP32, name must match a registered driver (case-sensitive) to return true; otherwise returns false.
On non-ESP32 platforms always returns false.

functions.name: CFastLED::isDriverEnabled
functions.description: ESP32: Queries whether a named channel driver is enabled. Non-ESP32: Always returns false.
requirements: On ESP32, name must be non-null and case-sensitive.
On non-ESP32 platforms always returns false.

functions.name: CFastLED::getDriverCount
functions.description: ESP32: Returns the number of registered channel drivers. Non-ESP32: Always returns 0.
requirements: None; platform-dependent return value.

functions.name: CFastLED::getDriverInfos
functions.description: ESP32: Returns a span describing all registered channel drivers (sorted by priority). Span remains valid until the next call to any non-const method. Non-ESP32: Returns an empty span.
requirements: Do not persist the returned span beyond the next non-const method call on FastLED, as its backing storage may change.
On non-ESP32, expect an empty span.

functions.name: CFastLED::wait
functions.description: Waits for all channel bus transmissions to complete, polling the channel bus manager until READY. Uses delayMicroseconds(100) between polls to avoid watchdog timeouts. Safe no-op on platforms without a channel bus.
requirements: None; safe to call on all platforms.

functions.name: CFastLED::setMaxPowerInVoltsAndMilliamps
functions.description: Sets a maximum power budget in volts and milliamps; internally converted to milliwatts and used for dynamic brightness limiting.
requirements: volts is 8-bit (typical 5).
milliamps is a 32-bit value.
Effective limit is volts*milliamps milliwatts.

functions.name: CFastLED::setMaxPowerInMilliWatts
functions.description: Sets a maximum power budget in milliwatts and enables the power-limiting brightness function.
requirements: milliwatts must be a 32-bit non-negative value.

functions.name: CFastLED::setPowerModel
functions.description: Configures the RGB LED power consumption model for accurate power management calculations.
requirements: model must be a valid PowerModelRGB describing per-channel consumption and overhead.

functions.name: CFastLED::getPowerModel
functions.description: Returns the current RGB power consumption model used for power limiting.

functions.name: CFastLED::show
functions.description: Sends pixel data from all registered controllers to the LEDs using the specified brightness scale, updating engine events appropriately.
requirements: scale is an 8-bit value (0–255).
Controllers and buffers must have been registered via addLeds prior to calling.

functions.name: CFastLED::onEndFrame
functions.description: Called automatically at the end of show(). Triggers end-of-frame tracking and events.
requirements: Normally not called directly by user code; invoked by show().

functions.name: CFastLED::clear
functions.description: Clears all LED data buffers to off/black. Optionally writes the cleared data to the LEDs if writeData is true.
requirements: If writeData is true, hardware will be updated immediately which may affect timing constraints.

functions.name: CFastLED::clearData
functions.description: Clears only the local LED data buffers without writing to hardware.

functions.name: CFastLED::showColor
functions.description: Fills all controllers' LEDs with the specified color at the specified brightness scale and updates the hardware.
requirements: scale is an 8-bit value (0–255).

functions.name: CFastLED::delay
functions.description: Delays for the specified number of milliseconds. Continuously calls show() during the delay to drive the dithering engine (at least once).
requirements: ms is a millisecond duration; may trigger multiple show() calls during the interval.

functions.name: CFastLED::setTemperature
functions.description: Sets a global color temperature that overrides per-controller settings.
requirements: temp is a CRGB describing the target white balance/temperature.

functions.name: CFastLED::setCorrection
functions.description: Sets a global color correction that overrides per-controller settings.
requirements: correction is a CRGB describing per-channel correction factors.

functions.name: CFastLED::setDither
functions.description: Sets the global dithering mode for all controllers (e.g., BINARY_DITHER or DISABLE_DITHER).
requirements: ditherMode must be one of the defined dithering mode constants.

functions.name: CFastLED::setMaxRefreshRate
functions.signature: void CFastLED::setMaxRefreshRate(fl::u16 refresh, bool constrain = false)
functions.description: Sets a global maximum refresh rate (Hz). Attempts to call show() faster than this rate will block until permitted. If constrain is true, the rate is constrained to the slowest set so far.
requirements: Call after adding all controllers if you intend to override the default (which is the slowest of all added controllers).
refresh is a 16-bit frequency value in Hz.

functions.name: CFastLED::countFPS
functions.description: Tracks elapsed time over nFrames show cycles to compute frames-per-second (updates an internal FPS counter).
requirements: nFrames should be a positive integer; default is 25.

functions.name: CFastLED::getFPS
functions.description: Returns the most recently computed frames-per-second value.

functions.name: CFastLED::count
functions.description: Returns the number of registered LED controllers (strips) added via addLeds().

functions.name: CFastLED::operator[]
functions.description: Returns a reference to the x-th registered controller.
requirements: x should refer to an existing controller index in the range [0, count()). Passing an out-of-range index will lead to undefined behavior. (Inferred from typical operator[] semantics; explicit range behavior not documented.)

functions.name: CFastLED::size
functions.description: Returns the number of LEDs in the first registered controller.
requirements: At least one controller should be registered; otherwise return value behavior is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: CFastLED::leds
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the CRGB buffer of the first registered controller.
requirements: At least one controller should be registered; otherwise returned pointer validity is unspecified by this header.
Do not write beyond the buffer length reported by size().

functions.name: fl::cled_contoller_size
functions.description: Returns the size (in bytes) of the CLEDController object for introspection and tooling. Useful for diagnostics or ABI checks.
requirements: None; utility function for introspection.

data_types.description: An arbitrary byte string used as a C-style, null-terminated name when passed via std::string::c_str(). May contain any UTF-8 or binary data including embedded nulls; however, only the prefix up to the first null byte is considered by C APIs. Here it represents a driver name identifier (e.g., "RMT", "SPI", "PARLIO") on ESP32, but any string is accepted.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target datatype: string passed as C string for driver names on ESP32.
# Valid/interesting values should include known driver names, case variants,
# empty and long names, names with embedded NUL (though c_str will stop at NUL),
# unicode, and strings near typical limits. We return bytes; fuzzing framework
# will split/consume for FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.

KNOWN_NAMES = [
    b"RMT", b"SPI", b"PARLIO", b"I2S", b"SPI2", b"SPI3",
    b"rmt", b"spi", b"parlio",
    b"",  # empty name
    b"DEFAULT", b"ALL", b"NONE",
]

UNICODE_NAMES = [
    "驱动", "драйвер", "controlador", "pilote", "treiber", "driver",
    "ドライバ", "드라이버", "محرّك", "תַּדְפִּיס", "गति",
]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # mix of alnum and punctuation to exercise parsing paths
    alphabet = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_-.:,/#+@"
    return bytes(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _with_embedded_nul(r: random.Random, base: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not base:
        base = b"X"
    pos = r.randint(0, len(base))
    return base[:pos] + b"\x00" + base[pos:]


def _unicode_bytes(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    s = r.choice(UNICODE_NAMES)
    # randomly mix with ASCII tail/head
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        s = _rand_ascii(r, 0, 6).decode('ascii', 'ignore') + s
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        s = s + _rand_ascii(r, 0, 6).decode('ascii', 'ignore')
    return s.encode('utf-8')


def _repeat_name(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    base = r.choice(KNOWN_NAMES) if r.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ascii(r, 1, 6)
    reps = r.randint(2, 50)
    out = (base + b";") * reps
    return out[: min(len(out), 1024)]


def _case_variants(name: bytes) -> List[bytes]:
    try:
        s = name.decode('latin1')
    except Exception:
        return [name]
    return [
        s.upper().encode('latin1'),
        s.lower().encode('latin1'),
        s.title().encode('latin1'),
    ]


def _compose_inputs(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a sequence of candidate names separated by newlines so multiple
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can consume different slices if the harness does so.
    # Include length prefixes occasionally for frameworks that use them.
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Known names and their case variants
    base = r.choice(KNOWN_NAMES)
    parts.append(base)
    for v in _case_variants(base):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(v)

    # 2) Unicode variants
    if r.random() < 0.9:
        parts.append(_unicode_bytes(r))

    # 3) Random ASCII names of varying lengths
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 8))
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 9, 32))

    # 4) Very long name near typical limits
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 128, 512))

    # 5) Embedded NUL variants
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(_with_embedded_nul(r, _rand_ascii(r, 3, 12)))

    # 6) Repeated names pattern
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(_repeat_name(r))

    # 7) Edge cases
    parts.append(b"")  # empty
    parts.append(b"\x00")  # just NUL

    # Occasionally include length-prefixed blocks (uint16 len | data)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        blob = _rand_ascii(r, 0, 64)
        parts.append(struct.pack('<H', len(blob)) + blob)

    # Join with newlines; total length bounded to 4096
    data = b"\n".join(parts)
    return data[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return _compose_inputs(r)
